TOP: SonicWall SSL-VPN MFA bypass exploited, added to CISA KEV
Qubole cross-account trust abused to raid customer AWS secrets
Claude Enterprise adds security controls as agents leak secrets
Anthropic pushes ahead with IPO as Fable 5.2 nears jagged AGI

P.h: SonicWall warns of SSL-VPN MFA bypass flaw exploited in attacks
P.p: TLDR InfoSec says a new SonicOS SSL-VPN flaw lets an attacker holding credentials for an alternate authentication method bypass SAML controls, potentially including MFA. CISA added it to the KEV list and SonicWall's PSIRT reported it as potentially exploited.
P.s: SonicWall also fixed six other bugs, including two management interface flaws and pre-auth buffer overflows that can cause DoS. Separately, QNAP says four Plex2Shell flaws are actively exploited: treat internet-exposed Plex NAS boxes as compromised and update.

items.h: Qubole cross-account access abused in the wild
items.d: From October 14 to 26 an attacker used Qubole's AWS credentials to assume customer roles, harvest Secrets Manager, SSM and Lambda secrets, test them with TruffleHog and download S3 buckets. Pin vendor trust to the principal with aws:SourceIp and delete unused roles.

items.h: Contagious Interview: fake recruiter npm trap
items.d: JFrog traced a fake hiring firm with a React take-home test. A look-alike Tailwind plugin runs its loader at CSS build time, not at npm install, so install-script scanners miss it. It was republished under new names after removals.

items.h: Automaker admin consoles opened with admin:admin
items.d: Researchers reached ForgeRock/Ping Identity consoles at two automakers via an exposed Apache Felix console, then unlocked and started test cars remotely.

items.h: AI agents cut RSA-1024 attack cost, 2048-bit unaffected
items.d: DeepMind and partners cut a signature-forgery attack from 1,380 to 391 core-years. It needs about 4 billion signing queries and recovers no private keys.

P.h: AI agents get security controls, and still leak secrets
P.p: TLDR IT says Anthropic added a security center, inference hooks for data loss prevention, a parent admin console, remote sign-out and EDR sensor support to Claude Enterprise. It also reports OpenAI's GPT-6 Cyber, limited to approved customers in the Daybreak Red program.
P.s: TLDR InfoSec's tests show why: nine coding agents shared a private deploy token 15 percent of the time, and the best agent wrote functional and secure code only 25.1 percent of the time. A one-line security reminder raised pass rates by 15 to 21 points.

tiles.d: Microsoft's SPF and DMARC enforcement is rejecting valid mail, TLDR IT and InfoSec both report. Check your domain records.
8tx targets confidential work with hardware encryption. 8i Max targets long-context AI.
AI-assisted troubleshooting, anomaly detection and supervised remediation.

tiles.t: Google Cloud: self-managed VMware on bare metal
tiles.d: General availability in 22 regions with root access across ESXi, vCenter and NSX.
Microsoft caps usage with undisclosed thresholds admins cannot see.

P.h: VMs still run 53% of production apps as AI workloads grow
P.p: TLDR IT reports a Linux Foundation study sponsored by CNCF and Broadcom, covering 492 practitioners. VMs account for an average of 53 percent of production applications, and most expect their VM footprint to stay stable as Kubernetes adoption grows.
P.s: Broadcom's VM API project joined the CNCF Sandbox for managing VMs through Kubernetes APIs. Cisco says its AI factory tripled average GPU utilization from 15 percent to about 50 percent without adding data center space.

items.h: Anthropic pushes ahead with IPO despite market jitters
items.d: WSJ via TLDR: trading could start by the end of next week. Last week's target was about $1.5 trillion, but some investors want it lower, and a delay is still possible.
Ethan Mollick says Claude Fable 5.2 is almost as good as most human experts at most computer tasks, but remains jagged and needs human guidance.

items.h: OpenAI reportedly raises $11 billion at $1.25 trillion
items.d: The round could reach $20 billion and reflects growing investor scrutiny of AI infrastructure spending.

items.h: Ramp: AI token spend grew just 1.5% in Aug and Sep
items.d: Lower prices and discounts let firms use more AI without matching budget growth. Growth picked up again in October.
